title: The Quiet Vector
premise: Mirabel Thornbury investigates 'impossible accidents' on Meridian's Reach, a colony whose slow, subsidized death nobody in the Core wants to acknowledge. When a distress signal arrives in Vessic — a language extinct for two hundred years — he recognizes it because his late mother sang him lullabies in it, and realizes the colony's accidents were never accidents: someone is erasing evidence of a pre-colonial civilization buried beneath the ice. Racing a corporate salvage fleet to the relay at the edge of dead space, Mirabel must choose between selling the proof that would save the colonists and destroying it to protect the living descendants of the Vessic who still hide below. He broadcasts the signal himself, dooming his career but giving the colony a voice the Core cannot silence.
about_author: Ines Eriksen is a former maritime insurance adjuster from Tromsø who turned to science fiction after a decade of documenting disasters no one wanted to pay for. Her work explores what survives when institutions decide a place — or a people — is no longer worth the paperwork.

chapters.title: Actuarial Grace
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. On Meridian's Reach, Mirabel closes his fortieth impossible-accident file: a greenhouse collapse with no structural cause. The colony's administrator begs him to write it up as negligence so insurance will pay. Emotional beat: weary compassion; Mirabel notices the dead language carved into the greenhouse foundation and says nothing.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Deaths
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Reviewing two decades of claims, Mirabel maps the accidents against old survey charts and finds they cluster over an unmapped cavity beneath the ice. A Core auditor arrives to announce the colony's subsidy ends in eight months. Beat: quiet dread as Mirabel realizes the deaths are patterned, not random.

chapters.title: Lullaby in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel, with flashback. A damaged relay spits a repeating distress signal; linguistics AI identifies it as Vessic, extinct since the Purge of 2187. Mirabel recognizes the melody — his mother's lullabies. Beat: vertigo of identity; grief resurfacing as he wonders who she really was.

chapters.title: What Mother Left in the Walls
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Searching his mother's sealed effects, he finds a Vessic phrasebook annotated in her hand and a relay access key stamped with a symbol matching the greenhouse carvings. Beat: suspicion curdling into resolve — she knew, and she left him the thread.

chapters.title: The Company of Convenient Fires
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Halcyon Salvage's advance team lands, politely confiscating survey data and offering Mirabel a generous transfer. He declines. That night the archive burns. Beat: anger hardening into purpose; first open antagonism with the corporation.

chapters.title: Ice Over Voices
chapters.summary: POV Sefa Okonkwo, a colony hydrologist. Descending into a melt-shaft to trace water loss, Sefa finds a sealed Vessic door humming with power — and people behind it who should not exist. Beat: wonder and terror; the reader learns the extinct are not extinct.

chapters.title: The Underfolk
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The hidden community, descendants of Vessic survivors, has kept the relay alive for generations, waiting for a signal home that never came. Their elder, Ashen, refuses contact with surface authorities. Beat: belonging tested — Sefa must choose whom to tell.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Sefa brings him down secretly. Ashen tests him with the lullaby; Mirabel answers in broken Vessic learned from his mother. Beat: recognition and fragile trust — Mirabel learns his mother was Vessic-born, smuggled out before the Purge.

chapters.title: Signal, Interrupted
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The distress signal cuts off mid-cycle. Telemetry shows Halcyon ships inbound, six weeks out, carrying demolition charges disguised as relay parts. Beat: urgency spikes; the race structure locks in.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge of Dead Space
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The only transmitter strong enough to reach the Core honestly sits at Relay Nine, four days' skiff travel across dead space with failing life support. Ashen gives Mirabel the full Vessic archive. Beat: solemnity of inheritance; he accepts the burden.

chapters.title: Paperwork for Arson
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel en route. Decoding Halcyon's filed claims, he proves the corporation caused the original accidents to suppress seismic readings of the Vessic vaults. Beat: cold clarity — he now holds motive, means, and a deadline.

chapters.title: Dead Space, Living Doubt
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel, alone in the skiff. Life support fails; he records a confession-log for the colonists in case he dies, confronting his lifelong outsiderhood — half-Core, half-Vessic, fully neither. Beat: interior low point; identity stripped to essentials.

chapters.title: The Auditor's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. A Halcyon interceptor catches him; its captain, Dreyse, offers to let him live if he hands over the archive — the company will 'manage' the colony's story. Beat: temptation and refusal; Mirabel stalls, sabotages, escapes crippled but free.

chapters.title: What the Colony Chose
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Back on the surface, Halcyon agents round up colonists for 'evacuation.' Sefa reveals the underfolk to the community council; after bitter argument, the colonists vote to stand together rather than scatter. Beat: solidarity forged; stakes become collective.

chapters.title: Relay Nine
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. He reaches the derelict relay and finds it booby-trapped by Halcyon. Repairing it means broadcasting openly — every ship in dead space will hear, including the demolition fleet. Beat: point of no return; he begins transmission knowing it's a flare.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The Vessic archive goes out in the clear: songs, histories, and Halcyon's own claim files interleaved as evidence. Responses flood in — some horrified, some hostile, one from a Core archivist confirming the language is real. Beat: triumph shadowed by incoming threat.

chapters.title: The Fleet Arrives
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Halcyon's main force reaches Meridian's Reach and seizes the relay hub topside, demanding the underfolk's location. The colonists stonewall; Sefa is taken hostage as leverage. Beat: darkest hour; everything Mirabel built seems about to be erased.

chapters.title: Ashen's Answer
chapters.summary: POV Ashen. Rather than hide, the underfolk walk up into the light — hundreds of them, singing the lullaby in unison across the ice as colony drones stream it live. Halcyon's demolition order collapses under public exposure. Beat: catharsis; invisibility weaponized into presence.

chapters.title: Terms of Settlement
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Landing amid the standoff, Mirabel presents his investigator's dossier to the corporate tribunal and the watching Core media: every accident, every signature, Dreyse's own bargain recorded. Halcyon withdraws; the subsidy question becomes a rights question. Beat: justice through the very paperwork meant to bury the truth.

chapters.title: Requiem for a Number
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. At the memorial for the accident dead, names are read aloud in both Standard and Vessic for the first time. Mirabel finally grieves his mother properly, among people who can sing her songs back to him. Beat: mourning transmuted into belonging.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Months later: the colony renegotiated as a cultural preserve, underfolk and surface folk drafting a shared charter. Sefa, now liaison, teaches the first open Vessic class. Beat: cautious hope; identity rebuilt as something chosen, not hidden.

chapters.title: A Signal Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Leaving on a new commission, Mirabel pauses at Relay Nine's restored dish, which now carries the colony's voice outward nightly. He adds his mother's lullaby to the broadcast queue and signs his last report: cause of all prior losses — neglect; prognosis — recovery. Beat: resolution; the forgotten place speaks, and he finally belongs to it.
